text:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate detected on /v1/generate in inference-us-west (p95 latency spike + 503s) — correlating with multiple node NotReady events in 'inference-us-west-pool' at 1718459100 :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): seeing the alerts. dashboard shows tail latency up to 2.8s and 5xxs ~3% for the last 5m. customers with SLA alerts started paging.

sanjay: I can see kubelet restarts on 3 nodes: ip-10-0-14-21, ip-10-0-14-22, ip-10-0-14-33. Crashloop-ish around the gpu-driver health probe. Logs show repeated `nvidia-smi` timeouts.

henry: linking kube events: `kubelet: heartbeat timeout, NodeNotReady` -> followed by `container runtime error: containerd: failed to create task` on the inference runtime pods.

eva: customers reporting increased tail latency and some generation requests returning 503 early in our SLO checkers. I've raised a ticket to CS with the list.

maya (oncall): @sanjay can you paste the last kubelet logs for ip-10-0-14-21? also, runbook step 1: add annotation to route traffic away from pool if more than 2 nodes NotReady.

sanjay: paste of last lines:
```
May 15 10:38:11 kubelet[1234]: E0515 10:38:11.123 transient error: nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex failed, rv=999
May 15 10:38:11 kubelet[1234]: E0515 10:38:11.300 containerd: failed to start container: exit status 1
May 15 10:38:12 kernel: NVRM: GPU at 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
```
Looks like GPU driver losing device.

ops-bot: Automatic mitigation triggered: scaled inference-us-west-pool up by +2 nodes from autoscaler policy due to capacity drop.

maya (oncall): good. I'm going to cordon ip-10-0-14-21 and drain if it doesn't recover in 60s. We need to avoid more pod failures.

henry: quick check — any recent driver bundle rollout? deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: batch-roll gpu-driver/usw-2024-05-14 already rolled to 80% around 09:50 UTC`

maya (oncall): that matches timeframe. maybe the new driver is flaky on this kernel.

ryan: I'm starting a temporary routing rule to remove inference-us-west-pool from low-latency routing. That should send traffic to cross-region fallback (us-east) for new requests. Will keep warm cache hits in region.

eva: notifying our largest affected customers with a blameless note — queued message to customers with latency >1s.

maya (oncall): sanjay, proceed with cordon + drain plan. commands: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-14-21 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-14-21 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

sanjay: running now. drain started. a couple of pods are stuck in Terminating with `Error: containerd: container did not stop`.

henry: try `crictl ps -a` on the node and force `crictl rm` for stuck containers, then `systemctl restart containerd` if needed.

sanjay: did crictl rm on two stuck pods, restarted containerd. drain now completing. node goes NotReady briefly then back to Ready but GPU still flapping.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: Declared P2 (inference degradation) — paging escalation to SRE lead.

maya (oncall): I'm handing off to henry for deeper analysis — maya (oncall) -> henry (taking over). Handoff notes: autoscaler scaled +2, routing temporarily bumped to cross-region, cordoned/drained ip-10-0-14-21.

henry: taking over. next steps: repro on one node with driver rollback test and check kernel/driver compatibility matrix. Also prepare a fast rollback of gpu-driver to previous stable tag if we see the same failure on another node.

ryan: I will keep cross-region routing active until we confirm stability. Also bumped concurrency limit for us-east to avoid queueing.

eva: CS updated customer list; support is on standby. No data exfiltration concerns — just availability.

henry: collecting `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `dmesg` from the affected nodes. dmesg shows repeated `NVRM: Xid (79): GPU has fallen off the bus` errors.

maya (oncall): can we quick-rollback the driver? what's the process and ETA?

henry: rollback plan: 1) mark km-hosts managed-driver DaemonSet to previous image `gpu-driver:usw-2024-05-07`, 2) apply with `kubectl set image ds/gpu-driver gpu-driver=redwood/gpu-driver:usw-2024-05-07 --namespace kube-system` 3) watch `kubectl rollout status ds/gpu-driver -n kube-system` and ensure nodes stabilize. ETA ~10-15m for rollout, + ~5-10m for nodes to rejoin and pods to reschedule.

ops-bot: Running preflight: checking driver kube ds compatibility... result: warning — 2 nodes currently at risk of eviction during rollout.

sanjay: initiating image set now.

henry: rolling update in progress. Monitoring `kubectl get nodes` and inference pod restarts.

~8 minutes later~

sanjay: driver rollback applied, pods restarting. two previously flapping nodes came back to Ready and GPU health steady. p95 tail latency falling back to baseline ~220ms. 503s dropping to 0.2%.

incident-bot: UPDATE: alerts resolved for inference-us-west (p95 latency and 5xxs returned to normal).

maya (oncall): great work. henry, can you follow up with a postmortem note and vendor ticket for the driver regression? include CVE check but likely unrelated.

henry: will open a postmortem draft and include timeline, root cause hypothesis (driver regression causing GPU reset / Xid 79), mitigation steps (rollback, cordon/drain, cross-region reroute), and long-term fix: pin kernel-driver combos in rollout and add canary pool for driver DS.

eva: CS will send customer status update that issue is mitigated and we're doing a full RCA.

maya (oncall): closing handoff. If anything else flares, re-ping this thread. Thanks team :tada:

henry: postmortem draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4321 (will populate)

deploy-bot: NOTE: driver rollback triggered by henry at 1718459340 — image redwood/gpu-driver:usw-2024-05-07

maya (oncall): marking incident handled. final status: mitigated, root cause suspected driver regression (gpu-driver/usw-2024-05-14). follow-ups: vendor case, postmortem, add automated rollback on Xid>50 spike, create canary pool.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED at 1718459543
